# Part  1 - Data Processing

I'm going to use R's api functions to pull PUMS data down from the US Census website.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(httr)
library(jsonlite)
library(janitor)
```
## Parsing Variable Values (i.e. labels)
```{r}
variable_json <- httr::GET("https://api.census.gov/data/2021/acs/acs1/pums/variables.json")

#str(variable_json, max.level = 1)
parsed <- fromJSON(rawToChar(variable_json$content))
#parsed

variable_descriptions <- as_tibble(parsed)
variable_descriptions
saveRDS(variable_descriptions, file = "data/variable_descriptions.rds")
```


## Parsing API Data

```{r}
#, restrictions = c()  hard coded in as STATE=44 or REGION=1
helper <- function(year = 2024, vars = c(), restrictions = c()) {

  #Generate all the input parameters:
  address <- "https://api.census.gov/data/"
  
  #Check singularity and validity of the year
  if (length(year) != 1) {
    stop("Argument 'year' must be a single value, not a vector or list.")
  }
  if (!year %in% c(2021, 2022, 2023, 2024)) {
    stop("Argument 'year' must be ONE of the following: 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024.")
  }

  #Check the requested variables
  if (length(vars) == 0) {
    final_request_vars <- "AGEP,PWGTP,SEX"
  } else {
      vars_allowed <- c("AGEP", "GASP", "GRPIP", "JWAP", "JWDP", "JWMNP", "JWMNP", "PWGTP","FER","HHL","SCH","SCHL","SEX","ST","STATE","REGION","DIVISION")
      
      #Check to make sure all requested vars are allowed.
      #rlang::arg_match(vars, vars_allowed, multiple = TRUE)
      #stop("Dudeski, you chose variables that are not in our list. Please restrict to numeric variables: AGEP, GASP, GRPIP, JWAP, JWDP, JWMNP, and to categorical varailes: FER, HHL, SCH, SCHL, SEX.")
  
      #Create separate lists of geo, str, and num vars for further checking
      numeric_vars <- c("AGEP", "GASP", "GRPIP", "JWAP", "JWDP", "JWMNP", "JWMNP")
      string_vars  <- c("FER","HHL","SCH","SCHL","SEX")
      geography_vars<- c("ST","STATE","REGION","DIVISION")
      
      #Rename variable "ST" to "STATE" for years 2021 & 2022
  
      
      #Create separate lists of the requested variables for each type
       req_num_vars <- vars[vars %in% numeric_vars]
       req_str_vars <- vars[vars %in% string_vars]
       req_geo_vars <- vars[vars %in% geography_vars]
       
       #Push out defaults, in case nothing is listed
       if (length(req_num_vars) == 0) req_num_vars <- "AGEP"
       if (length(req_str_vars) == 0) req_str_vars <- "SEX"
       if (length(req_geo_vars) == 0) req_geo_vars <- "STATE"
       
       #Glue the requested variable strings all together
       final_request_vars <- paste(req_num_vars,req_str_vars,req_geo_vars,"PWGTP", sep = ",")
  }
browser()
  #Subset the API Request, so as not to get too much data.
  if (length(restrictions) == 0) {
    message("Broski, that's too much data. Census will cut you off. We are going to trim that down to just STATE:44 (because Rhode Island is awesome) and go from there. You can cange this by adding a geographic variable (STATE/ST, REGION, etc.) or some other restriction to the `restrictions` parameter.")
    final_restrict <- "&for=STATE:44"
  } else {
      if(restrict_var %in% geography_vars) {
        restrictions <- sub("[=].*", ":.*", restrictions)
        final_restrict <- paste0("&for=",restrictions)
      }
      else final_restrict <- paste0("&",restrictions)
  }




  #Call API and parse result
  final_api <- paste0(address,year,"/acs/acs1/pums?get=",final_request_vars,final_restrict,"&key=541a25ef175ec8d1abf1a4b9bb864ac88cf70e54")

  variable_json <- httr::GET(final_api)
  parsed <- fromJSON(rawToChar(variable_json$content))

  #Make API result into tibble, save it, and display it in the log
  api_result <- parsed |>
    janitor::row_to_names(row_number = 1) |>
    as_tibble()|>
    type_convert()
  View(api_result)
  return(api_result)
}

yr2020x<- helper(year = 2020)  #Should fail, year out of range.
yr2024a <- helper()             #Default vars, year.
yr2024b <- helper(year = 2024, vars=c("AGEP", "SEX"))  #Should still work
yr2024c <- helper(year = 2024, vars=c("AGEP", "SEX"), restrict = "SEX = 1")  #Should still work
yr2021x <- helper(year = 2021)  #Should fail, because of ST vs STATE.
yr2021a <- helper(vars=c("AGEP", "BAS"))  #shouldn't work.

yr2024 <- helper(vars = "GASP")
yr2022 <- helper(year = 2022, vars = c("GASP","GRPIP")) 
yr2022b<- helper(year = 2022, vars = c("AGEP", "SEX")) #Won't work because ST in 2022

```
